idiom_name: struct with synthesized memberwise initializer + argument labels
implementation_notes: Swift structs are value types and the compiler synthesizes the memberwise initializer from the stored properties, so `DrawParams(x: 2, y: 3)` already is the parameter object with named construction; default property values become default arguments of that initializer, and `Equatable`/`Hashable` conformance is synthesized on request. Classes remain the classic form only when reference identity, inheritance or deinitialization is genuinely required.
pitfalls: The memberwise initializer is internal and disappears once an initializer is declared in the type's body; put custom initializers in an extension to keep it.
Struct value semantics mean the callee receives a copy: mutations are lost unless the parameter is `inout`, unlike class-based argument passing.
Argument labels are part of the call syntax, so renaming a stored property is a source-breaking change for every call site.
